answer: The kernel test I would run is signed bricklayer apprenticeship record with construction authority attestation: a record the construction authority kept across a completed apprenticeship, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the violet of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head. The canyon is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
